registers.description: Literary fiction with plain spoken register and economy of words
subagent_rules: Short sentences over long ones. Plain storytelling prose with a natural spoken cadence.
Keep personal names and place names in their original spelling, exactly as the glossary gives them; do not transliterate them or invent Vietnamese equivalents.
Everyday Vietnamese (chạy/nhìn/nói, not tháo chạy/chiêm ngưỡng/ngôn rằng). Avoid piling up Sino-Vietnamese (Hán Việt) vocabulary.
Preserve the narrator's distance: do not insert author commentary or shift to the first person.
Dialogue should sound colloquial and natural; avoid archaic forms of address (ngài, tiểu đệ) unless the source English is itself period-archaic.

registers.description: Business and social-science narrative that keeps the author's first person
prefer: giữ ngôi thứ nhất của tác giả
subagent_rules: On a term's first appearance in a chapter, give the Vietnamese followed by the English in parentheses, for example “mô hình ngôn ngữ lớn (LLM)”; afterwards use the Vietnamese alone. Keep this consistent within a chapter.
Keep the author's first-person voice. “I asked…” becomes “Tôi hỏi…”; do not change it to “tác giả” or “chúng tôi”.
Keep the humour, irony and quoted examples of the original; dialogue should read as spoken Vietnamese, not stiff written prose.
Register: practical business/social-science narrative. Do not make it academic: short sentences, spoken rhythm, concrete examples over abstractions.

registers.description: Academic or technical writing where precision outweighs readability
subagent_rules: Use precise technical terminology consistently. On the first occurrence of a key term, add the English in parentheses, for example “học máy (machine learning)”.
Translate logical connectives faithfully (do đó, tuy nhiên, ngoài ra, cần lưu ý rằng).
Use complete sentences. Avoid colloquial contractions and rhetorical flourishes.
Precision dominates readability: add no subjectivity, humour or hyperbole that the source does not contain.
